//: Insolvia's brand colours — the ONE place they are written down.
These are OVERRIDES, layered on top of the installed @insolvia-ai/tokens
rather than replacing it. From 0.5.0 the design system's base theme is
deliberately monochrome and states no brand at all, so the brand belongs to
the consumer and this file is the consumer.
THE PALETTE IS WARM NEUTRAL, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE IDEA. There is no brand
colour in the interface. Every level of hierarchy is carried by type scale,
weight, and a step on the warm grey ramp — which is what lets a screen hold
a lot of information and still read as calm. The navy-and-brass palette this
replaced put three competing accents on every screen: a saturated ground, a
brass CTA, and coloured status pills, none of which were the thing you were
meant to look at.
The neutrals sit at a hue of about 90 degrees — warm, barely chromatic —
with slightly more chroma in the light steps so whites stay clean, and less
in the dark ones so they never shift brown.
`accent` is the one thread of the old identity that survives, and it is used
in exactly one place: the dot after the wordmark. Anywhere else it would be
the only saturated thing on the screen, which is the problem this palette
exists to remove.
STATUS COLOURS ARE OVERRIDDEN HERE, which the package's own default would
not need. The base ships saturated green, amber and red — correct for a
monochrome chrome, and wrong against this one, where they would be the only
vivid marks on an otherwise neutral page and would read as decoration rather
than as signal. These are the same three hues held to the ramp's chroma.
Note the app leans on WORDS for status first ('Blocked', 'Complete') and on
these colours second, so a reader who cannot use hue loses nothing.
`primary` is a dark warm grey rather than the ground's near-black, so its
hover and active states have somewhere to go: the web derives them by
darkening with color-mix, and a #0F0E0D button cannot get darker.
`primaryHover` / `primaryActive` / `accentHover` are DERIVED states, here
for React Native only — on web they are color-mix over the base role, so the
CSS output omits them (see tool/render-brand-theme.ts).
Shape lives in brand/radii.json and typefaces in brand/fonts.json, both
generated by the same tool and gated by the same `npm run tokens:check`.
DO NOT hand-copy these values into an app. Every consumer is generated
from this file by `npm run tokens`, and `npm run tokens:check` fails the
build when one has drifted.
The decision, and what to do if a second brand ever appears:
docs/adr/0020-the-brand-is-a-consumer-owned-override.md
